verifications.claim: Trump Accounts (530A accounts) are tax-advantaged investment accounts for children under 18.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Trump Accounts — or 530A investment accounts — a new tax-advantaged savings and investment program designed to give American children a financial head start.' R2: 'designed for children under 18 who have a Social Security number.' R3: 'special rules for beneficiaries under the age of 18.' R4: 'designed to help children build long-term wealth.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly describe Trump Accounts (530A) as tax-advantaged investment/savings accounts for children under 18.

verifications.claim: Trump Accounts (530A accounts) offer a federal $1,000 "seed" contribution for children born between 2025 and 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Each child born from last year until the end of 2028... will receive $1,000 in seed funding.' R2: 'The $1,000 seed funding is available to babies... born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028.' R3/R4: identical exact dates and $1,000 government seed.
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm the $1,000 federal seed for children born 2025-2028; R1 contextually matches dates.

verifications.claim: Parents can open Trump Accounts (530A accounts) to invest up to $5,000 annually in US stock index funds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Families can add another $5,000 per year.' R2: 'annual contributions are capped at $5,000... invested in... mutual funds or ETFs that track an index of primarily U.S. companies, like the S&P 500.' R3/R4: $5,000 annual limit and U.S. stock index funds/ETFs.
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly support parents/families opening accounts with $5,000 annual contributions invested in U.S. stock index funds/ETFs.

verifications.claim: Funds in Trump Accounts (530A accounts) are tax-deferred until age 18.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'investments grow tax deferred until the child reaches adulthood.' R3: 'funds inside the account grow tax deferred... No withdrawals... until... age of 18.' R4: 'tax-deferred growth.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm tax-deferred growth with no access until age 18/adulthood.

verifications.claim: Children born between Jan 1, 2025, and Dec 31, 2028, qualify for an initial $1,000 from the government, notes WHYY and this YouTube video.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1 (WHYY): 'Each child born from last year until the end of 2028... $1,000 in seed funding.' R2/R3/R4: 'born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028... $1,000 government seed.'
verifications.reasoning: WHYY (R1) supports with contextual dates; others directly match exact dates and $1,000.

verifications.claim: Families can contribute up to $5,000 annually per child, notes ERS Texas (.gov) and this YouTube video.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4 (ERS Texas): '$5,000 per year.' R1/R2/R3: confirm $5,000 annual family/parent contributions.
verifications.reasoning: ERS Texas (R4) directly states $5,000 per year; corroborated by others.

verifications.claim: Parents can file IRS Form 4547 during the 2026 tax season for children born in 2025.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '2026 tax season... file IRS Form 4547 along with their federal tax return.' R2: 'elect to open... using IRS Form 4547... by the April 15 tax deadline this year.' R3: 'File Form 4547 with your tax return.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Form 4547 filing with taxes in 2026 context for newborns like 2025 births.

verifications.claim: Funds in Trump Accounts (530A accounts) are locked until the child turns 18, notes the National Association of REALTORS® and this YouTube video.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 (NAR): 'can’t be withdrawn before Jan. 1 of the calendar year in which the child turns 18.' R1: no withdrawals implied until adulthood. R3: 'No withdrawals are permitted until January 1 of the year the child reaches the age of 18.'
verifications.reasoning: NAR (R2) directly states locked until 18; others support.

verifications.claim: Funds in Trump Accounts (530A accounts) are intended for expenses such as higher education or a first-time home purchase, notes the National Association of REALTORS® and this YouTube video.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 (NAR): 'used on certain expenses—like higher education or a first-time home purchase—without... penalty.' R1: 'paying for college or buying a home.' R3/R4: similar qualified uses without penalty.
verifications.reasoning: NAR (R2) directly lists higher education and first-time home purchase; others confirm.

verifications.claim: Trump Accounts (530A accounts) can be requested via tax forms.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2/R3: 'file IRS Form 4547... with their federal tax return' or 'File Form 4547 with your tax return.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm requesting/opening via IRS tax form 4547.

verifications.claim: An official enrollment portal is set to launch in summer 2026, says the National Association of REALTORS® and this YouTube video.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 (NAR): 'sign up on the official trumpaccounts.gov website this summer.' R1: 'initiate... May 2026... activation... July 4, 2026.' R3: 'Enroll... at trumpaccounts.gov... contributions... July 5, 2026.'
verifications.reasoning: NAR (R2) states summer launch; R1/R3 confirm portal and summer 2026 timeline.

verifications.claim: Trump Accounts (530A accounts) are designed to operate similarly to IRAs.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'new type of individual retirement account (IRA).' R3: 'similar to traditional individual retirement accounts (IRAs).' R4: 'starter retirement account.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe similarity to or as a type of IRA.

verifications.claim: Trump Accounts (530A accounts) must be invested in low-cost US stock index mutual funds or ETFs, according to ERS Texas (.gov) and this YouTube video.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4 (ERS Texas): 'limited to U.S. stock index funds... S&P 500 index fund.' R2: 'mutual funds or exchange traded funds (ETFs) that track an index of primarily U.S. companies, like the S&P 500.' R3: 'mutual funds or exchange-traded funds that track the S&P 500 or another index of primarily American equities.'
verifications.reasoning: ERS Texas (R4) and others confirm requirement for U.S. stock index mutual funds/ETFs, but none specify 'low-cost'; supported in broader terms.
